strengths: The paper contributes a simple, useful approach to difficult three-view pose problems: generate virtual correspondences from image-point centroids, apply established 5-/6-point and P3P solvers, and refine using the real observations. This is a meaningful methodological contribution with a low implementation barrier.

The calibrated-camera results demonstrate useful accuracy–runtime trade-offs. On PhotoTourism (Table 2), 4p3v(M±δ)+R+F achieves AUC@10 of 70.47 in 75.78 ms, versus 70.54 in 105.50 ms for 5pt+P3P. The faster 4p3v(M)+R+F achieves 69.06 in 30.54 ms, outperforming the homotopy baseline's 66.63 in 76.45 ms.

Evaluation is substantial: PhotoTourism and Cambridge Landmarks, 5,000 triplets per scene, two RANSAC frameworks, fixed-iteration accuracy–runtime curves, noise and outlier experiments, and refinement/offset ablations. The supplementary evaluation includes all three camera pairs, strengthening evidence that the gains extend beyond the main paper's chosen error metric.

The manuscript explicitly acknowledges approximation, scene dependence, and the limited benefit of learning after refinement. The supported practical contribution for calibrated cameras provides a stronger case for acceptance than rejection, despite the reservations below.
weaknesses: The geometric justification provides limited guidance about reliability. Section 7 bounds virtual-match epipolar error by the triangle's radius; this does not establish small pose error or a reliable refinement initialization. Table 1 shows substantial initialization degradation—for example, median error on Trevi Fountain is 25.9° versus 12.3° for the five-point solver outside RANSAC. Dependence on depth variation, baseline, and overlap is not systematically characterized, limiting predictability beyond the evaluated scenes.

The shared-focal-length extension has weaker practical support. In Table 3, 4p3vf(M) obtains AUC@10 of 49.88 at 12.67 ms, versus 56.79 at 11.72 ms for 6pt+P3P. Requiring fewer correspondences is potentially valuable, but the reported real-data results do not establish a favorable accuracy–runtime regime for this extension. Focal-length estimation error is also unreported.

The learned component offers little demonstrated practical benefit. On PhotoTourism, 4p3v(L)+R obtains AUC@10 of 69.88 at 297.88 ms, compared with 69.90 at 74.94 ms for 4p3v(M)+R. Its preliminary status is appropriately acknowledged, but the demonstrated contribution rests primarily on the deterministic construction.

Technical specification and reproducibility have unresolved issues. Equation (2) defines a signed residual without an absolute value or square; minimizing this expression as written need not reduce epipolar discrepancy. The exact training objective therefore remains unclear. Code is promised without a supplied link, and important implementation settings, including numerical RANSAC inlier thresholds, are not fully specified. These concerns particularly affect reproduction of the learned branch.

The comparison with the epipole-search baseline [35] is indirect and inconsistently reported. The main text says its oracle performs worse than the proposed oracles, whereas Section 9.7 and Table 7 report better accuracy. Footnote 6 attributes the discrepancy to an adjustment of RANSAC termination without specifying that adjustment. This is a secondary reporting and comparison weakness; it does not invalidate the stronger evidence against the implemented five-point and homotopy baselines.
